doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

chapter: Meeting Joe and life with the Basie band
title: Following the Basie band and riding the Basie bus
summary: She travelled with the band before marrying Joe; she kept to her niche on the bus with its assigned seats and shared the trips with Rigmor Newman.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But when you married him he was with the Basie band.

Not actually when we were married, no. But we had been going around together for several years when he was in the Basie band. So there was a certain amount of traveling with the band and following the band and getting to know everyone.
Tell us about the Basie bus.

Oh, the Basie bus was wonderful. I was always very cognizant of the fact that a woman on the bus is like a bump on a log. You know, that’s the band’s home, it’s where they can get off stage and relax and say what they want to say and do what they want to do. And having a strange woman there was really something they didn’t need. So one tried to stay in your own little niche you know? I tried to stay with Joe and always sit in the right place, because everybody had assigned seats and you didn’t sit over there because that was Sonny Payne’s seat, you didn’t sit here because that was Marshall Royal’s row, and so on. So I tried to stay out of it. But they were always so tolerant. Nobody every made me feel a nuisance you know. You know I inflicted that on myself in fact I think. But I also had the company of Joe Newman’s wife, Rigmor, and so there were two of us traveling and we had a wonderful time. We ate tuna out of the can and champagne out of paper cups and it was a great education and great fun.
